comment: Overall, Dr. Stevenson was a nice professor who cared about his students, but he expected too much for an introductory level class. We had seven tests throughout the semester, which made it very difficult, even though the lowest was dropped. He often went into depth on topics we didn't need for exams and barely covered ones we did need to know.

He's an extremely caring and genuine person, but I wouldn't recommend his style of teaching for those who have no prior exposure to chemistry. He goes into the weeds a bit and lectures aren't always intuitive, so you do have to put in work outside of class to grasp the concepts.

Pre labs and lab reports so much work and he goes through the material so fast in class you actually have to read the textbook. Don't know why this is a gen ed class when the content is hard. He tries to help but its just so much work. be prepared to spend hours doing chem work. would take a class with HIM, not chem, again

Definitely take for Chem 300! He provides so much practice material, making it easy to succeed in his class. You need to practice the excel material regularly in order to do well, but he helps with that by reviewing screencast material in class. I will say, he is a tough grader and sometimes the grading criteria is unclear. But amazing prof!
Avoid at all costs. He is the most unreasonable professor in the chemistry department. So much work outside of class and grading is extremely tough.

Dr. Stevenson is a great guy, very funny, and understands that Chem 110 isn't for chem geniuses. The content is difficult but he definitely explains it in a non-chem major way. Tests are hard but you get a cheat sheet.

Good prof for Chem/Envr 110. Tests are difficult but he makes review material very accessible online & they're semi-open note. Notes are super well organized & straightforward; classes are mostly learning new concepts for note-taking. Material is quite relevant, prof presents it in a lively and intuitive way. A little too quick for me but its chill
Enjoy the excellent lectures!!! He is open and knowledgeable. Definitely take his class again!

Just please don't teach this lab with excel. 
:((((((((((((((

Though some of the grade is built into small assignments, tests are the majority of the grade. He is not particularly helpful outside of class, and his grading on tests are super stringent. He is very helpful with staying on top of the material through the cheat-sheets he assigns, however, and he has all his lectures accessible through screencasts.
Although this man is an olympic level swimmer, he is a terrible person and I hate him.

Nice guy terrible teacher.  No matter what I did (and I did go in for help after tests) he never liked what I wrote on the tests.  No idea how he chooses to grade.  Class is very dependent on tests and the group work is pointless but necessary to get a decent grade.
Steves is a good teacher but the material is just so tough. He does what he can to make it bearable. A nice guy too if you get to know him. Sometimes he's too smart for the class to follow

DO NOT take Pollutants in the Environment with Dr. Stevenson. He is a nice guy but makes this class much harder than it should be for non-science majors. It is clear that he cares very little about the class in comparison with his others, and he takes forever to grade things
Stevenson is super helpful, really wants you to do well. You do have to do the readings but the hws you do you get to use on tests which makes tests much easier. An A is def attainable for anyone.

it is a very interesting class that gives a good overview of environmental issues. there is a lot of reading but you get to use the summary sheets you make on the tests. 3 tests and 1 term paper.  he is a boring professor sometimes

Major reading, at least two lengthy articles per class with questions and summaries that can be used on tests. Takes attendance only on days with group presentations, about 1 a week. Tests are impossible he uses keys and if your answer doesn't have certain words than you lose points. only take the class if you like reading and summaries every class
this class is pretty straightforward. reading every night followed by summaries that you get to use on tests. he's a nice guy and he keeps the material pretty simple

He's a tough nut to crack. Can be pretty demanding of his students. But he's an awesome professor. Did an awesome job of teaching the stats class and make 8:15's bareable. Great lab prof, but tough grader.

This teacher confused me more than helped me. He would spend an entire lecture on something really confusing and then sorta tell us we didn't need to know it (which, upon futher questioning, meant that we didn't need to know it at all). His review sessions are sometimes just him telling us to look it up in the book. I would recommend somebody else.
Genuine interest in the student
My god worst prof ever.  Does not read emails you send him and then questions you later about what should have been taken care of.  This man is off his rocker and should not be here anymore!

Dr. Stevenson was a great teacher who obviously enjoys teaching. Every so often he would come up with something amusing (and mildly bloody) to explain some analytical chemistry technique (you think I'm kidding, but he compared absorption spectroscopy with soldiers in a minefield...). Take Stevo!
Great teacher definately knows his stuff.  He also lets you know what is going to be on tests unlike other professors who are vague at best.  Got me interested in a possible env minor
pretty easy class, he goes off on tangents a lot, but he def knows his stuff
No Comments
started all right, instruction degraded as the year went on
